docs.title: Install
docs.text: version 0.51.0

docs.title: VTTinker
docs.text: A browser extension for Roll20. It raises the zoom limits, draws the grid past the map edge, lets you add your own token markers, and fixes the chat footer. Each tool has its own on/off switch.

docs.title: Firefox signed
docs.text:
Signed by Mozilla. Install it once and Firefox keeps it.

Download .xpi

docs.title: Chrome developer mode
docs.text:
Not on the Chrome Web Store, so it loads as an unpacked extension.

Download .zip

docs.title: Install on Firefox
docs.text:
1. Download the .xpi file.
  2. Open it. If nothing happens, go to about:addons, click the gear icon, choose Install Add-on From File, and pick the downloaded file.
  3. Accept the permission request. There is one: storage.
  4. Open a Roll20 game. A VTTK section appears at the bottom of the left toolbar.

docs.title: Install on Chrome
docs.text:
1. Download the .zip and extract it to a folder you intend to keep. Chrome reads that folder on every startup.
  2. Go to chrome://extensions and turn on Developer mode.
  3. Click Load unpacked and select the extracted folder, the one containing manifest.json.
  4. Open a Roll20 game. The VTTK section appears in the toolbar.

Developer mode

Chrome shows a warning banner at startup and may disable unpacked extensions when you reset your profile. Reload the folder if that happens.

docs.title: Access
docs.text:
Permissions storage Sites app.roll20.net/editor Network none, except images you add as markers Written to Roll20 token status markers you place Stored locally your settings and marker palette

Source: github.com/igneefleur/vttinker

docs.title: Features
docs.text: Four tools, each with its own switch in the VTTK section of the toolbar.

docs.title: Zoom range
docs.text:
Roll20 stops at 10% and 250%. Set your own minimum and maximum. The mouse wheel, the buttons and the slider all respect them.

Inside Roll20's own range nothing is intercepted. Past it, the step size matches Roll20's last step, so the transition is not noticeable.

docs.title: Grid beyond the page
docs.text:
Roll20 stops drawing the grid at the page edge. This continues it for a chosen number of cells, aligned with the existing grid.

All five grid types work: square, hex by column, hex by row, isometric, dimetric. Roll20's own drawing code is reused rather than reimplemented.

docs.title: Custom markers
docs.text:
Roll20 ships 47 token status markers. Add your own with any image URL.

Other players see them without installing anything. The marker is written to the game as a normal status marker, with the image address in the tag, so Roll20 draws it for everyone.

Markers can be applied to several tokens at once, carry a counter, and are reorderable by drag.

docs.title: Chat footer
docs.text:
Fixes the vertical alignment of the bottom row, where the sender select and the Send button sat at different heights. Adds an emoji picker.

The emoji are standard Unicode, in the eight official groups. Everyone can read them.

docs.title: Roll20's two renderers
docs.text:
Roll20 runs two rendering engines behind the same interface: the current one (Jumpgate) and the legacy one, still used by older campaigns.

All four tools work on both, as GM and as player. Each combination was tested on a live game.

docs.title: Cost
docs.text:
Per frame, all tools on 0.2 ms CPU 3.5% of one core Frame rate 181 → 176 fps

Measured on a live game. The drawing layer only runs when a tool has something to draw; otherwise it is not in the page at all.

docs.title: Do the other players need it too?
docs.text:
No.

A marker you place is written to the game as a regular Roll20 status marker. Roll20 draws it, not the extension, and the image address travels in the tag. Everyone sees it.

Same for emoji: they are standard Unicode characters.

The zoom range, the extended grid and the chat layout only affect your own view.

docs.title: Why does Chrome need developer mode?
docs.text:
The extension is not published on the Chrome Web Store. Chrome only installs store items in one click; anything else goes through Load unpacked, which requires developer mode.

Firefox accepts a signed extension without going through its store, which is why there is an .xpi on one side and a .zip on the other.

docs.title: What leaves my machine?
docs.text:
Nothing. There is no fetch, no XMLHttpRequest, no sendBeacon anywhere in the code. A test in the build checks this on every change.

The exception is the one you create: if you add a marker pointing at an image, your browser fetches that image from the host you gave.

Worth knowing

If another player at your table places a custom marker, your browser fetches their image from their host, and that host sees your IP address. This is true of any image shared in a game. The extension sends no referrer.

docs.title: Does it slow Roll20 down?
docs.text:
With all four tools on: 0.2 ms per frame, 3.5% of one core, 181 → 176 fps.

The drawing layer only runs when there is something to draw.

docs.title: Does it work on older campaigns?
docs.text: Yes. Roll20 runs two rendering engines; all four tools work on both, as GM and as player.

docs.title: How do I uninstall it?
docs.text:
Through your browser's add-on manager. Your settings go with it.

Markers you placed on tokens stay in the game — they belong to Roll20, not to the extension. Remove them from the tokens to clear them.

docs.title: Can I read the code?
docs.text:
Yes: github.com/igneefleur/vttinker.

It is written in French, comments included. The code is readable; it is not open source.
